sentence: Choose the standard written completion that describes this large difference: The lift is ___ faster.
setupText: Using the lift takes one minute; using the stairs takes five.
taskText: Choose the standard written completion that describes this large difference: The lift is ___ faster.
text: Using the lift takes one minute; using the stairs takes five. Choose the standard written completion that describes this large difference: The lift is ___ faster.
options: very
much
a little
as
answer: much
focusKey: coverage-comparatives-a2-741:Much strengthening a comparative
explanation: Much can strengthen a comparative: much faster describes a large speed difference.

rationales.much: Much can strengthen a comparative: much faster describes a large speed difference.
rationales.very: Very normally modifies the basic adjective, as in very fast, not very faster.
rationales.a little: A little faster describes a small difference, not the large one specified.
rationales.as: As needs the basic adjective and another as for equality; as faster does not fit.

sentence: Choose the completion for a formal report that compares the number received: I received ___ emails today than yesterday.
setupText: You received twelve emails yesterday and eight today.
taskText: Choose the completion for a formal report that compares the number received: I received ___ emails today than yesterday.
text: You received twelve emails yesterday and eight today. Choose the completion for a formal report that compares the number received: I received ___ emails today than yesterday.
options: less
fewer
fewest
more
answer: fewer
focusKey: coverage-comparatives-a2-742:Fewer for discrete counts in formal writing
explanation: Emails can be counted separately; fewer expresses the lower number in formal written English.

rationales.less: Less with plural counts occurs in conversation, but fewer is the conventional choice for separate countable emails in this formal report.
rationales.fewer: Emails can be counted separately; fewer expresses the lower number in formal written English.
rationales.fewest: Fewest identifies the lowest number in a group, not this direct than comparison.
rationales.more: More gives the opposite quantity relation: eight is below twelve.

sentence: Which reply answers 'Which departure shall we choose?'
setupText: Trains leave at 7:15, 7:40, and 8:05. You want to leave as early as possible.
taskText: Which reply answers 'Which departure shall we choose?'
text: Trains leave at 7:15, 7:40, and 8:05. You want to leave as early as possible. Which reply answers 'Which departure shall we choose?'
options: The latest one, at 8:05.
The middle one, at 7:40.
The earliest one, at 7:15.
A later one, at 7:40.
answer: The earliest one, at 7:15.
focusKey: coverage-comparatives-a2-743:Earliest in a practical three-way choice
explanation: Earliest selects the first departure in the whole list, which is 7:15.

Latest selects the last departure; the stated aim is to leave early.
The middle departure is not the first available departure.
Earliest selects the first departure in the whole list, which is 7:15.
Later compares this departure with an earlier one; it does not meet the earliest-departure goal.

sentence: Choose the grammatically correct completion: The online map is ___ than the paper map.
setupText: You are comparing two maps for planning a walk.
taskText: Choose the grammatically correct completion: The online map is ___ than the paper map.
text: You are comparing two maps for planning a walk. Choose the grammatically correct completion: The online map is ___ than the paper map.
options: useful
as useful
the most useful
more useful
answer: more useful
focusKey: coverage-comparatives-a2-744:More plus a longer adjective
explanation: Useful forms this comparative with more; than introduces the paper map as the comparison point.

rationales.useful: Useful alone does not form the direct comparison introduced by than.
rationales.as useful: Equality would need as useful as, not as useful than.
rationales.the most useful: The most useful ranks within a group; it does not fit before than here.
rationales.more useful: Useful forms this comparative with more; than introduces the paper map as the comparison point.

sentence: Which description preserves that ranking?
setupText: Among four nearby hotels, the Park Hotel has the lowest room price.
taskText: Which description preserves that ranking?
text: Among four nearby hotels, the Park Hotel has the lowest room price. Which description preserves that ranking?
options: It is the least expensive of the four.
It is less expensive than one of the others.
It is the most expensive of the four.
It is as expensive as the other three.
answer: It is the least expensive of the four.
focusKey: coverage-comparatives-a2-745:Least versus less and full-group ranking
explanation: Least expensive ranks the hotel lowest in cost among all four.

Least expensive ranks the hotel lowest in cost among all four.
rationales.It is less expensive than one of the oth: This only compares it with one hotel; it does not preserve its lowest-price ranking across all four.
Most expensive gives the highest price, reversing the ranking.
As expensive as gives equality, not the lowest price.

sentence: Choose the grammatically correct completion: The case with wheels is easier ___ through the station.
setupText: One suitcase has wheels; the other must be lifted.
taskText: Choose the grammatically correct completion: The case with wheels is easier ___ through the station.
text: One suitcase has wheels; the other must be lifted. Choose the grammatically correct completion: The case with wheels is easier ___ through the station.
options: moving
move
for move
to move
answer: to move
focusKey: coverage-comparatives-a2-746:An infinitive specifying the dimension of easier
explanation: Easier to move compares the effort needed for moving the case.

rationales.moving: After easier, an infinitive identifies the action made easier: easier to move.
rationales.to move: Easier to move compares the effort needed for moving the case.
rationales.move: The bare verb move needs to after easier in this construction.
rationales.for move: For cannot introduce the bare verb move after easier.

sentence: Choose the grammatically correct completion: Ren checks the totals ___ than I do.
setupText: A supervisor is comparing how two assistants check invoices.
taskText: Choose the grammatically correct completion: Ren checks the totals ___ than I do.
text: A supervisor is comparing how two assistants check invoices. Choose the grammatically correct completion: Ren checks the totals ___ than I do.
options: more carefully
more careful
as carefully
most carefully
answer: more carefully
focusKey: coverage-comparatives-a2-747:Comparative of a manner adverb
explanation: More carefully compares the manner of checking; than I do supplies the other person's action.

rationales.more careful: Checks needs a manner adverb here; more careful would describe a person or thing.
rationales.as carefully: An equality comparison needs as carefully as, not as carefully than.
rationales.more carefully: More carefully compares the manner of checking; than I do supplies the other person's action.
rationales.most carefully: Most carefully is a superlative; the direct than comparison needs more carefully.

sentence: How does B compare the notices?
setupText: A: 'Can you read the new notice?' B: 'A little more clearly, but I still need my glasses.'
taskText: How does B compare the notices?
text: A: 'Can you read the new notice?' B: 'A little more clearly, but I still need my glasses.' How does B compare the notices?
options: The new one is much harder to read.
The two are equally easy to read.
The new one is much easier to read.
The new one is slightly easier to read.
answer: The new one is slightly easier to read.
focusKey: coverage-comparatives-a2-748:A little modifying comparative improvement
explanation: A little more clearly reports a small improvement; the glasses are still needed.

More clearly describes improvement, and a little describes a small amount.
More clearly indicates a difference, even though it is small.
Much overstates the size of the improvement expressed by a little.
A little more clearly reports a small improvement; the glasses are still needed.

sentence: What change does Jo describe?
setupText: The heating has stopped. 'It's getting colder and colder in here,' says Jo.
taskText: What change does Jo describe?
text: The heating has stopped. 'It's getting colder and colder in here,' says Jo. What change does Jo describe?
options: The room is colder than every other room.
The room stays at the same low temperature.
The room keeps becoming colder.
The room alternates between cold and warm.
answer: The room keeps becoming colder.
focusKey: coverage-comparatives-a2-749:Comparative and comparative for continuing change
explanation: Repeating the comparative with and describes a continuing change in one direction.

Repeating the comparative with and describes a continuing change in one direction.
rationales.The room is colder than every other room: Colder and colder tracks change over time; it does not rank this room against all others.
rationales.The room stays at the same low temperatu: Getting colder and colder means the temperature is changing, not staying the same.
rationales.The room alternates between cold and war: The repeated colder points in one direction, not back and forth.

sentence: What is Mia comparing its performance with?
setupText: After trying a repaired phone, Mia says, 'It works better than I expected.'
taskText: What is Mia comparing its performance with?
text: After trying a repaired phone, Mia says, 'It works better than I expected.' What is Mia comparing its performance with?
options: The performance of every new phone
Its performance before it was repaired
The price she paid for the repair
Her earlier idea of how it would work
answer: Her earlier idea of how it would work
focusKey: coverage-comparatives-a2-750:A than-clause naming an expectation
explanation: Than I expected compares actual performance with the performance Mia had imagined.

rationales.The performance of every new phone: The sentence gives her expectation as the comparison point, not all new phones.
rationales.Her earlier idea of how it would work: Than I expected compares actual performance with the performance Mia had imagined.
rationales.Its performance before it was repaired: That may matter to Mia, but than I expected does not name the earlier performance as its standard.
rationales.The price she paid for the repair: The comparison concerns how it works, not the cost of the repair.

sentence: Choose the grammatically correct completion: You leave home earlier than I ___.
setupText: You and a colleague drive the same route to work.
taskText: Choose the grammatically correct completion: You leave home earlier than I ___.
text: You and a colleague drive the same route to work. Choose the grammatically correct completion: You leave home earlier than I ___.
options: am
do
have
does
answer: do
focusKey: coverage-comparatives-a2-751:Do substituting for an action in a comparative clause
explanation: Do stands for leave home, avoiding repetition of the action in the comparison.

rationales.am: Am cannot replace the ordinary verb leave in this comparison.
rationales.have: Have does not replace the simple present leave without a participle.
rationales.do: Do stands for leave home, avoiding repetition of the action in the comparison.
rationales.does: The subject I takes do, not does.

sentence: Complete the sentence correctly: Our team has ___ people as theirs.
setupText: Both teams have six people.
taskText: Complete the sentence correctly: Our team has ___ people as theirs.
text: Both teams have six people. Complete the sentence correctly: Our team has ___ people as theirs.
options: as many
as much
more
the most
answer: as many
focusKey: coverage-comparatives-a2-752:As many ... as for equal counts
explanation: As many ... as expresses equal numbers of countable people.

rationales.as much: People is plural and countable, so this equal-number comparison uses many.
rationales.more: More would need than, and it would describe unequal numbers.
rationales.the most: The most ranks a number above others; it does not complete an as equality pattern.
rationales.as many: As many ... as expresses equal numbers of countable people.

sentence: Which description matches the change?
setupText: Eight new people joined the evening class in May, twelve in June, and sixteen in July.
taskText: Which description matches the change?
text: Eight new people joined the evening class in May, twelve in June, and sixteen in July. Which description matches the change?
options: Fewer and fewer people are joining the class.
Just as many people join each month.
More and more people are joining the class.
The number joining each month is falling.
answer: More and more people are joining the class.
focusKey: coverage-comparatives-a2-753:More and more with a plural quantity
explanation: More and more plus a plural noun describes an increasing count; the monthly numbers of new arrivals rise.

rationales.More and more people are joining the cla: More and more plus a plural noun describes an increasing count; the monthly numbers of new arrivals rise.
rationales.Fewer and fewer people are joining the c: Fewer and fewer describes declining new arrivals, but the monthly counts increase.
Just as many suggests equal monthly numbers, not eight, twelve, and sixteen.
rationales.The number joining each month is falling: Falling gives the opposite trend to the rising counts of new members.

sentence: Choose the sentence that expresses the price relationship.
setupText: The basic chair costs $40. The office chair costs $80.
taskText: Choose the sentence that expresses the price relationship.
text: The basic chair costs $40. The office chair costs $80. Choose the sentence that expresses the price relationship.
options: The office chair is half as expensive as the basic chair.
The basic chair is twice as expensive as the office chair.
The office chair is twice as expensive as the basic chair.
The chairs are equally expensive.
answer: The office chair is twice as expensive as the basic chair.
focusKey: coverage-comparatives-a2-754:Twice as ... as
explanation: Twice as expensive means two times the price: eighty dollars compared with forty.

rationales.The office chair is half as expensive as: Half would make it twenty dollars; eighty is double forty.
rationales.The office chair is twice as expensive a: Twice as expensive means two times the price: eighty dollars compared with forty.
rationales.The basic chair is twice as expensive as: This reverses which chair has the double price.
Their prices are eighty and forty, not equal.

sentence: Which sentence keeps the same comparison?
setupText: A walking guide says, 'The road is more dangerous than the river path.'
taskText: Which sentence keeps the same comparison?
text: A walking guide says, 'The road is more dangerous than the river path.' Which sentence keeps the same comparison?
options: The river path is less dangerous than the road.
The river path is more dangerous than the road.
The road is as dangerous as the river path.
The road is less dangerous than the river path.
answer: The river path is less dangerous than the road.
focusKey: coverage-comparatives-a2-755:Reversing compared terms with more and less
explanation: Reversing the order of the routes requires less in place of more to preserve the relation.

rationales.The river path is more dangerous than th: This swaps the danger ranking between the routes.
rationales.The road is as dangerous as the river pa: As dangerous as would describe equal danger, not the difference stated.
rationales.The river path is less dangerous than th: Reversing the order of the routes requires less in place of more to preserve the relation.
rationales.The road is less dangerous than the rive: This keeps the route order but reverses more to less, changing the meaning.

sentence: What does B tell A to choose?
setupText: A: 'Which application form should I use?' B: 'The shorter of the two.'
taskText: What does B tell A to choose?
text: A: 'Which application form should I use?' B: 'The shorter of the two.' What does B tell A to choose?
options: A form that is short compared with most forms
Either form, because both have the same length
The form that is less long than the other form
The form with more pages than the other
answer: The form that is less long than the other form
focusKey: coverage-comparatives-a2-756:The comparative of the two as a selection phrase
explanation: The shorter of the two selects one member of this pair by relative length.

rationales.A form that is short compared with most: The shorter of the two compares only these forms; it does not compare them with most forms.
rationales.Either form, because both have the same: Shorter distinguishes their lengths rather than saying they match.
rationales.The form with more pages than the other: More pages would normally make it the longer option, not the shorter one.
rationales.The form that is less long than the othe: The shorter of the two selects one member of this pair by relative length.

sentence: Which statement matches the tutor's comparison?
setupText: The tutor says, 'The online exercise is just as easy as the paper one.'
taskText: Which statement matches the tutor's comparison?
text: The tutor says, 'The online exercise is just as easy as the paper one.' Which statement matches the tutor's comparison?
options: The two exercises have the same difficulty.
The online exercise is slightly easier.
The paper exercise is much easier.
The online exercise is only for beginners.
answer: The two exercises have the same difficulty.
focusKey: coverage-comparatives-a2-757:Just strengthening equality
explanation: Just strengthens the equality in as easy as; neither exercise is described as harder.

rationales.The two exercises have the same difficul: Just strengthens the equality in as easy as; neither exercise is described as harder.
Just as easy as expresses equality, not a small advantage.
The sentence does not give the paper exercise an advantage.
rationales.The online exercise is only for beginner: Just modifies the equality comparison; it does not restrict who may do the exercise.

sentence: Complete the comparison with the right possession: Our printer is noisier than ___.
setupText: You work in Finance. Sales has a noisy printer, but the printer in your department makes even more noise.
taskText: Complete the comparison with the right possession: Our printer is noisier than ___.
text: You work in Finance. Sales has a noisy printer, but the printer in your department makes even more noise. Complete the comparison with the right possession: Our printer is noisier than ___.
options: their
theirs
they
them
answer: theirs
focusKey: coverage-comparatives-a2-758:Possessive pronoun for the compared object
explanation: Theirs can stand for their printer, keeping a printer-to-printer comparison without repeating the noun.

rationales.their: Their needs a noun after it, such as their printer.
rationales.theirs: Theirs can stand for their printer, keeping a printer-to-printer comparison without repeating the noun.
rationales.they: They refers to the people and does not replace their printer here.
rationales.them: Them would compare the printer with the people, not with their printer.

sentence: Which description matches the bookings, not the tour length?
setupText: All three tours last two hours. The museum tour has the lowest number of bookings.
taskText: Which description matches the bookings, not the tour length?
text: All three tours last two hours. The museum tour has the lowest number of bookings. Which description matches the bookings, not the tour length?
options: The museum tour is the shortest.
The museum tour is the least popular.
The museum tour is the most popular.
The museum tour is as popular as the others.
answer: The museum tour is the least popular.
focusKey: coverage-comparatives-a2-759:Selecting the dimension and direction of a superlative
explanation: Least popular describes the tour attracting the fewest bookings in this group.

Shortest compares length or duration; all the tours last two hours.
Most popular would fit the highest number of bookings, not the lowest.
Least popular describes the tour attracting the fewest bookings in this group.
rationales.The museum tour is as popular as the oth: As popular as would describe equal popularity rather than the lowest booking count.

sentence: What does the walker mean?
setupText: A walker says, 'This route is longer than it looks on the map.'
taskText: What does the walker mean?
text: A walker says, 'This route is longer than it looks on the map.' What does the walker mean?
options: The route is shorter than the walker expected from the map.
The map shows a different route from the one being walked.
The route is the longest one shown on the map.
The map makes the route seem shorter than it really is.
answer: The map makes the route seem shorter than it really is.
focusKey: coverage-comparatives-a2-760:Actual degree versus apparent degree
explanation: The comparison contrasts actual length with apparent length, so the apparent length is lower.

rationales.The route is shorter than the walker exp: Longer than it looks says the actual route exceeds the apparent length, not falls below it.
rationales.The map shows a different route from the: The sentence compares apparent and actual length; it does not say they are different routes.
rationales.The route is the longest one shown on th: Longer than it looks does not rank this route against other routes.
rationales.The map makes the route seem shorter tha: The comparison contrasts actual length with apparent length, so the apparent length is lower.
